findings.where: Screen 3, Worked at 100 µF panel (first line)
findings.what: The main winding's R 15 Ω and X 18 Ω never appear on the page, so 9.82 A and 50.2° cannot be checked. The ratio's 6.00 A and 30.1° are used with no line showing them either. Add the lines: Z = √(36² + 13.2²) = 38.34 Ω, 230 ÷ 38.34 = 6.00 A, arctan(13.2 ÷ 36) = 20.1°, 50.2 − 20.1 = 30.1°.

findings.where: Screen 3, Worked at 100 µF panel (Torque ratio line)
findings.what: The rule on screen says torque goes with Im × Is × sin(angle), but the ratio line drops Im without a word. Add one line: the main current is 9.82 A in both cases, so it cancels.

findings.where: Screen 3 Line current readout and screen 5 bars (15.3 A, 12.4 A)
findings.what: No rule for the line current is shown anywhere on the page. Add one plain line to the worked panel: the line current is the two winding currents added as phasors, which gives 15.3 A without the capacitor and 12.4 A with 100 µF.

findings.where: Screen 3, live sentence under the readouts (below and above the peak)
findings.what: "A bigger capacitor still lets more current through than it loses in angle, so the torque still rises" and "A bigger capacitor now closes the angle faster than it adds current, so the torque falls" weigh current against angle, so they need two reads. Split each into two plain sentences, e.g. "A bigger capacitor lets more current through. Here that gains more torque than the narrower angle loses."

findings.where: Screen 3, the note under the readouts
findings.what: The screen carries about 91 words of prose, plus a nine-line worked panel, and is by far the longest scroll at 360 px. "So the torque peaks near 120 µF, not at 90°" also mixes µF with degrees. Cut the note to two sentences, e.g. "The most torque comes near 120 µF, with the currents about 70° apart, not 90°. Example values, not a maker's." Move the windings to the worked panel.

The screen runs to 96 words, over the 90-word limit for a SHOW screen. Trim, for example by dropping "Once running, it carries on", which the card's trap already says, or by shortening the switch row.

findings.where: Screen 2 and Keep this card, What it is for
findings.what: These say the currents are "nearly 90° apart", but the card's rule says about 80° and the example gives 77.6°. Say about 80° throughout so the card agrees with itself.

The question gives both the bulging case and the 38 µF reading, which makes the answer obvious. A fairer find would give the symptom and one clue. The hint for "main winding is open" could also say how to rule it out on test: resistance of the run winding.
"That is this lesson." talks about the lesson itself. Say what it does instead, e.g. "That is how this motor gets its strong start."

On a real job he would want the discharge figures (about 20 kΩ, 5 W, five seconds) and an acceptable tolerance band (±20% in one guide, ±10% in another) on the card itself. Today it only says "through a resistor" and "tolerance marked on it".

The best bridge from his trade is lesson.analogy: the same leading current he uses for power factor correction, here used to push one winding ahead. The steps screens never show it. One sentence on screen 2 would start from what he knows.

No check asks about the picture's cause: capacitor size changes the angle and the current, and so the torque. The duty-rating check is the one the brief asked for. If a fourth check would be too many, the read sentence could at least ask him to predict what a capacitor twice the size does.
"Once the rotor turns, one winding makes torque on its own" corrects the momentum slip by assertion only. Neither this lesson nor lesson 4 says why it can, so a skeptical reader is left asking.

findings.where: lesson.explain and lesson.practice (shown only if the frame fails)
findings.what: Together they carry 18 footnotes, several on plain statements such as "The main winding's current still lags.[^9]". Keep only the few he would look up on a job: switch speed, discharge resistor, tolerance.
